title: Why Apple's Third Co-Founder Sold 10% for $800 After 12 Days
alt_title_1: Ronald Wayne's 1976 Exit: Uncapped Downside Kills Big Upside
alt_title_2: How Personal Liability Forced Ronald Wayne Out of Apple
description_hook: On April 1, 1976, Ronald Wayne typed Apple Computer's original partnership agreement for a 10% stake alongside Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak. Twelve days later, fearing unlimited partnership debt liability, he sold his 10% for $800.

scenes.headline: Apple's Third Co-Founder Cashed Out for $800
scenes.stat_label: SOLD 10% OF APPLE AFTER JUST 12 DAYS (APRIL 1976)
bullets: Typed Apple's April 1, 1976 contract for a 10% stake
Withdrew April 12 for $800, plus $1,500 later that year
scenes.narration: On April 1, 1976, forty-one-year-old draftsman Ronald Wayne typed Apple Computer's partnership contract for a ten percent stake, then sold his entire share twelve days later for eight hundred dollars, plus fifteen hundred later.
scenes.source: Apple Computer Partnership Withdrawal (Apr 12, 1976); Ronald Wayne (2011)

scenes.headline: Why Unlimited Liability Scared Only One Partner
scenes.left_body: Early twenties with near-zero assets for creditors to seize
scenes.right_body: Personal savings + failed slot-machine debt scars + full liability
scenes.narration: Early Apple was a general partnership carrying unlimited personal liability. Young Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak owned almost nothing creditors could seize, whereas Wayne held personal assets and remembered paying off debts from a failed slot-machine venture.
scenes.source: Apple Computer Partnership Withdrawal (Apr 12, 1976); Ronald Wayne (2011)

scenes.headline: Unshielded Downside Forces Early Exits
scenes.stat_label: HOW FAST PERSONAL RUIN KILLS PATIENCE
bullets: Jobs took credit parts orders that exposed Wayne's savings
Uncapped downside forces smart operators out of big upside
scenes.narration: Once Jobs ordered parts on credit, Wayne knew unpaid supplier bills could legally drain his personal savings. Unshielded downside risk forces rational people out of generational upside.
scenes.source: Apple Computer Partnership Withdrawal (Apr 12, 1976); Ronald Wayne (2011)

scenes.headline: Ring-Fence Liability So You Can Stay in the Game
scenes.stat_label: CAPPED DOWNSIDE ENABLES MULTI-DECADE HOLDING POWER
scenes.stat_subtext: LLC shield + zero personal debt + surplus cash -> calm patience
scenes.narration: Ring-fence every asymmetric venture inside capped legal liability, refuse personal debt guarantees, and fund high-upside bets strictly with surplus cash your household bills never require.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Apple Partnership Withdrawal (1976)

scenes.headline: Cap Your Ruin Before Chasing Asymmetric Returns
scenes.stat_label: PATIENCE IS BUILT ON LEGAL AND FINANCIAL SHIELDS
bullets: Separate business risk from family housing and cash reserves
Size volatile bets so a zero never changes your lifestyle
scenes.narration: Cap your personal ruin upfront, because you can only hold ten-year compounders when worst-case losses cannot touch your survival.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Apple Partnership Withdrawal (1976)
